name: text-to-cad
one_liner: Lets you describe a physical object in plain words and get back a real 3D design file you could 3D print, laser cut, or send to a manufacturer.
buyer: An Etsy or Shopify seller of custom physical products (phone stands, jewelry, nameplates) who wants to turn customer requests into sellable, manufacturable designs without hiring a CAD designer.
business_use_cases: A small print-on-demand shop lets customers describe a custom part in a form, auto-generates the CAD file, and sends it straight to a 3D printing service for fulfillment.
A product inventor turns a sketch or idea into a manufacturing-ready file and gets instant design-for-manufacturing checks before paying for a prototype run.
A freelance product designer speeds up client work by generating first-draft CAD models from a client brief, then refining by hand.

money_ideas.idea: Run a 'describe it, we print it' custom physical product shop: customers type what they want, you generate and 3D print it, charge per item.
Offer an 'instant prototype' service for inventors: text-to-CAD plus a connection to a CNC or 3D-printing partner, charging a markup on each manufactured part.

steal_this: This weekend, set up a simple web form where people describe a custom keychain or phone stand, auto-generate the CAD file, and offer to 3D print and ship it for a flat fee.
